clue.text: Geek from small school

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A nerdy pupil from a tiny school.
explanation.definitionFit: Spod is British slang for a dull, studious swot, much the same as a nerd.

clue.text: On which net hangs in Centre Court

parts.note: in football a centre is a ball played across into the middle, also called a cross
the bar is the court or tribunal where barristers plead

explanation.surface: Something at Wimbledon's Centre Court that holds up the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis surface misleads: the net in question is a goal's, which hangs from the bar across its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal's netting is fixed to the horizontal bar between the posts, so it hangs on it.

clue.text: No more work for retail outlet

parts.note: sh is the call to stop talking, saying no more
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A store that closes for good, leaving no more jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A store selling goods to the public is the basic retail outlet.

clue.text: Star lost set after a chance

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word straight behind the a
something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A star player lost a set after taking a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like the player, but it is the printed symbol; 'lost' scrambles set and 'after' puts it behind a.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed star symbol used to mark a footnote is called by this name.

clue.text: Summary one takes off copper

parts.note: an aper is one who apes, mimicking or taking off others
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A digest of how someone removed some copper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief outline or quick summary of a subject.

clue.text: See man (coach) read out name

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Look, a man, a coach, reading out a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese; the cleric belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior cleric serves under a bishop within a diocese, or see.

clue.text: Good start for game

parts.note: to rouse game is to start it, make it break cover

explanation.surface: A good beginning to the match.
explanation.definitionFit: This moorland bird is shot for sport, so it is game in the hunting sense.

clue.text: Contract office boss

indicators.note: to contract a word is to shorten it, here losing its final letter

parts.note: a study is a room for working, a home office

explanation.surface: A deal signed by the head of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not the manager but a raised knob or ornamental stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or nail head, the same as an ornamental stud.

clue.text: Place for Australian Open with no covers: right hot

indicators.note: covers are the outer letters, so taking them away leaves only the inside

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A venue for the Australian Open, uncovered, with the sun beating down.
explanation.definitionFit: This Western Australian state capital is a city in Australia, a place for Australians.

clue.text: On grass, ace for McEnroe?

indicators.note: on joins the two, putting the word for ace against the word for grass

parts.note: ace as an adjective means excellent, superb
to grass is to inform, to rat

explanation.surface: On a grass court, an ace served by John McEnroe.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this was the tabloid nickname for the famously tantrum-prone John McEnroe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloids nicknamed the tennis player John McEnroe this for his tantrums on court.

clue.text: Salvation Army supply pre-paid envelopes to drop off

indicators.note: envelopes as a verb means wraps around, so one piece goes inside the other
supply read as supple, bendy, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The charity hands out stamped envelopes for people to drop off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' (read as supple) rearranges pre-paid, and 'envelopes' is the verb, wrapping that round SA.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off can mean to vanish from view, to vanish from sight or records.

clue.text: See 23
Husband (Tramp) repeatedly covers meat not on barbecue

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so the doubled pair sits either side of the meat
repeatedly says the pair of letters is given twice

parts.note: Tramp is the setter's name, so the setter is I

indicators.note: not means the following word is taken out

parts.note: bacon is cured pork meat

explanation.surface: The setter's husband keeps covering meat that isn't on the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' is the setter, so it gives I; 'repeatedly' doubles HI and 'covers' wraps the pair round the trimmed meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibachi is a small Japanese charcoal grill, a kind of portable barbecue.

clue.text: Beat champion in tie

parts.note: to beat is to hit

explanation.surface: Defeating the champion in a tennis tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up or fasten something is to hitch it, as with a horse.

clue.text: Forcibly take mad McEnroe away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters have wandered off and come back in another order

explanation.surface: Drag the raging McEnroe off court by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize something for official use, taking it by force.

clue.text: Rubbish tennis player in America

indicators.note: in places the player's name inside the letters for America

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, America
Monica Seles was a champion tennis player

explanation.surface: A dismal tennis player competing in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish used as an adjective means worthless or no good at all.

clue.text: A queen wearing sister's dresses

indicators.note: wearing means the letters for sister have the others on, round them

parts.note: sis is short for sister
R is the abbreviation for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A queen trying on her sister's frocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a draped garment worn by South Asian women, a type of dress.

clue.text: American through to final of slam gets beat

parts.note: thru is the American spelling of through

indicators.note: final of points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An American player reaches a Grand Slam final and wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to strum or drum rhythmically, to beat out a steady sound.

clue.text: Andy Murray's traditional outfit has no length for tackle

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is dropped

parts.note: Murray is Scottish, and the kilt is traditional Scottish dress

explanation.surface: The Scottish player's national dress is too short for the sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear or equipment, as in fishing tackle, which is kit.

clue.text: It's rising? Country ignoring national water level

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up
ignoring means a letter is left out

parts.note: Denmark is a European country

explanation.surface: Is the sea creeping up? A country is ignoring the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IT into TI; 'ignoring' removes N from DENMARK, leaving DEMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left by high water, showing the level it reached.

clue.text: Cringe to be in debt, going into credit

indicators.note: going into places the debt word inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: Wincing at going overdrawn when you expected credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink back in fear, as when one cringes.

clue.text: Sense hard tie: pull out

parts.note: wit is good sense
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a draw is a tied match

explanation.surface: Faced with a tough match, common sense says retire.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a contest is to retire from it, quitting before the end.

clue.text: Backs out of space by us: he backs things on wheels

indicators.note: backs as a verb means goes backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
the backs are each word's last letters, and out of says they are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone reversing out of a parking space beside a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs out of' strips the last letter from each of space, by, us, he, leaving SPACBUH; 'backs' then turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubcaps are the metal covers fitted over the centres of car wheels.

clue.text: Bachelor and host drunk with Sue Barker

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A single man and a tipsy host out with the presenter Sue Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Barker is a British former tennis player who long presented the BBC's Wimbledon coverage; here 'Barker' means a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a dog, and this short-legged long-eared hound is one breed.

clue.text: Very humid round part of South Africa

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
humid air is damp, wet
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Steamy weather around the south of the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is a large township near Johannesburg, an area of South Africa.

clue.text: Chips in, cooking: goes out with sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to date someone is to go out with them
food that is cooking is on

explanation.surface: Someone makes chips while their partner brings sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to contribute money, which is to give it as a gift.

clue.text: Coached British and took drugs

parts.note: used is slang for took drugs

explanation.surface: A British player was coached and caught doping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coached' is not trained but carried by coach, a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To be coached in this sense is to be carried by coach, a bus.

clue.text: Love child

definitions.meaning: an affectionate form of address, like darling or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A child born out of wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a pet name for a lover and an informal word for a baby.

clue.text: Place for tennis elbow: mind needing treatment

indicators.note: needing treatment says the letters are worked on and put into a new order

explanation.surface: Somewhere to treat tennis elbow, mind it gets seen to.
explanation.definitionFit: The All England Club in this London suburb hosts the grass-court championships.

clue.text: Left one tie

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: One tie left over.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes is to fasten or tie them up.

clue.text: Never taking part in Australian Open

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who has never played at Melbourne Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic ways to refuse, a slangy no meaning not ever.

clue.text: Does one work for queen? Worker to exploit queen

parts.note: a worker bee
an exploit is a feat, a daring deed
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Does a worker bee exploit its queen?
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters, the Yeomen Warders, guard the Tower of London on the monarch's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen Warders serve the sovereign at the Tower, a royal guard in Tudor uniform.

clue.text: Cold butter at front of picnic hamper

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a ram butts, so it is a butter

indicators.note: front of points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cold butter at the top of the picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' is not the basket but the verb to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp someone is to restrict them, as in cramping one's style.
